assessments.rationale: This option leverages secondary raw materials to reduce the material footprint (o) (Page 2) and incorporates recycled content (k) (Page 33). The lightweight ribbing aligns with parameter (t) (lightweight design) on Page 80, which emphasizes the 'reduction of material consumption, load- and stress-optimisation of structures, [and] use of lower density... materials' to achieve material savings and waste reduction.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (injection molding of rPP with complex ribbing requires tighter process controls and may increase cycle times) and Use Phase (rPP has lower scratch resistance and tensile strength than virgin ABS, potentially impacting aesthetic durability).

assessments.recommendation: Reversible snap-fits and standardized metal screws
assessments.rationale: This option directly supports design for recycling (d) by enabling non-destructive disassembly. As detailed on Page 79, ease of repair, upgrading, and reuse is expressed through 'ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly' and the 'use of standard components' without requiring specialized tools. This also facilitates the 'incorporation of used components' (k) and clean material separation at end-of-life.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (increases assembly steps and part count, raising production costs) and Use Phase (vibrations during operation may loosen screws, requiring user maintenance).

assessments.recommendation: Lightweight high-efficiency brushless DC (BLDC) motor with recycled copper windings
assessments.rationale: This choice aligns with parameter (t) (lightweight design) on Page 80 by reducing material consumption and utilizing high-strength, lower-density designs. Sourcing recycled copper windings supports parameter (h) (recycled content) and reduces the material footprint (o) (Page 2). Avoiding critical raw materials or hazardous substances ensures the motor does not complicate the recycling process (Page 35).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Sourcing (sourcing high-purity recycled copper and rare-earth magnets is highly complex) and Use Phase (requires complex electronic controllers which are vulnerable to electrical failures).

According to Page 79, ease of repair, reuse, and remanufacturing is enhanced by 'modularity', 'ease of non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly', and a reduced 'number and complexity of processes'. Modular blocks allow individual components to be harvested, refurbished, or cleanly recycled.

options_evaluated: Removable, modular battery pack using hazard-free chemistry
assessments.rationale: This option addresses parameter (f) (use of substances of concern) and (m) (environmental footprint). Page 9 and Page 35 emphasize minimizing substances of concern that make the recycling process 'more complicated, costly, environmentally impactful, or energy- or resource-demanding'. Eliminating the battery avoids hazardous battery chemistries, dramatically reduces the product's environmental footprint (m) (Page 33), and prevents premature product obsolescence due to battery degradation.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase (significantly reduces user mobility and convenience compared to cordless options) and Sourcing (requires sourcing long copper cables, which increases raw material weight).
